nodes.name: RF reactive magnetron sputtering at 303K
nodes.procedure: Tungsten trioxide thin films were grown on glass and indium tin oxide (ITO) coated glass substrates by RF magnetron sputtering technique by sputtering of pure metallic tungsten (50 mm diameter and 1 mm thick) target at a fixed sputter power of 150 W. The vacuum pumping system employed for sputter deposition was a combination of diffusion and rotary pumps capable to achieve an ultimate pressure of 4×10^-4 Pa. Pure oxygen and argon were used as reactive and sputter gases respectively. Fixed quantities of oxygen and argon gases were admitted into the sputter chamber through fine controlled needle valves and their flow rates were monitored individually by employing Aalborg mass flow controllers. The films were formed at substrate temperature of 303 K and fixed oxygen partial pressure of 6×10^-2 Pa and sputter pressure of 4 Pa.
nodes.source_text: Tungsten trioxide thin films were grown on glass and indium tin oxide (ITO) coated glass substrates by RF magnetron sputtering technique... The films were formed at different substrate temperatures in the range 303–673 K and fixed all other parameters as constant.

nodes.description: Electrochromic cyclic voltammetry testing in 1 M Li2SO4
nodes.source_text: As the substrate temperature increased to 473 K, the cathodic peak increased from -0.30 to -0.35 mA/cm² and anodic peak increased from 0.11 to 0.16 mA/cm², a small cathodic voltage peak observed at 0.29 V... diffusion coefficient of 1.85×10^{-11} cm²/s... The films formed at substrate temperature of 473 K exhibited better optical transmittance modulation of 40%... with a color efficiency of 33.8 cm²/C

nodes.description: Electrochromic cyclic voltammetry testing in 1 M Li2SO4
nodes.source_text: At higher substrate temperature of 573 K, the cathodic and anodic current densities decreased to -0.08 mA/cm² and 0.053 mA/cm² respectively... the diffusion coefficient decreased to 8.3×10^{-12} cm²/s... Further increase of substrate temperature to 573 K it decreased to 20%

nodes.characterization_summary: Films at 303 K are X-ray amorphous; films at ≥473 K show orthorhombic WO3 phase with (020) peak at 23.8° and additional peaks at 673 K; crystallite size increases from 17 to 24 nm from 473 to 673 K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The films deposited at 303 K do not contain diffraction peaks related to ${ \sf W O } _ { 3 }$ indicated that the films were of X-ray amorphous ... The crystallite size of the films increased from 17 to $2 4 \mathrm { n m }$ with increase of substrate temperature from 473 to 673 K respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: 303 K films show W=O stretch at 960 cm⁻¹ (amorphous); ≥473 K films show O-W-O stretches at 801 and 690 cm⁻¹ with intensity increase and W=O/O-W-O ratio decrease at 673 K.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the figure it is observed that the films deposited at 303 K, a broad absorption band observed at $9 6 0 \mathrm { c m } ^ { - 1 }$ was attributed to the stretching vibration of ${ \cal W } = 0$ bond ... As the substrate temperature further increased to 673 K the intensity of the O–W–O band increased and the ratio of ${ \cal W } = 0$ to O–W–O was decreased.

nodes.characterization_summary: Grain size increases from 80 nm (303 K, tiny uniform grains), 120 nm (473 K, void-free), to 140 nm (673 K, agglomerated denser films).
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen that the films have smooth surface and contains uniformly distributed tiny grains with average grain size of about $8 0 \mathrm { n m }$ at $3 0 3 \mathrm { K } .$ ... When the substrate temperature increased to 673 K, the agglomeration of grains takes place ... with average grain size of about $1 4 0 ~ \mathrm { { n m } }$.
